history.summary:
Cricket has evolved from its early origins in southeast England during the 16th century into a major global sport played across multiple formats including Test matches, One Day Internationals (ODIs), and Twenty20s (T20s). Codified formally with the establishment of the Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC) in the 18th century, the sport spread globally through the British Empire, establishing deep roots in the Indian subcontinent, Australasia, the Caribbean, and Southern Africa. 

The modern era has witnessed massive commercial expansion, broadcast innovation, and the birth of domestic T20 leagues worldwide. Governed internationally by the ICC, cricket balances the rich traditional heritage of multi-day Test cricket with the fast-paced, high-revenue spectacle of shorter formats, captivating billions of fans across all continents today in 2026.

key_eras.description: Characterized by legendary amateurs and professionals like W.G. Grace and Don Bradman, establishing Test match rivalries primarily between England, Australia, and South Africa.

Expansion of Test cricket to the West Indies, India, Pakistan, and New Zealand, culminating in Kerry Packer's World Series Cricket which modernized broadcasting, colored clothing, and player remuneration.
The rise of limited-overs World Cups, legendary fast-bowling dynasties, batting innovators like Sachin Tendulkar and Brian Lara, and the globalization of the game.
The explosive rise of Twenty20 leagues like the IPL, advanced tactical data analytics, multi-format dominance, and women's cricket reaching unprecedented professional milestones by 2026.
